title: Should film-makers be using AI?
description:
Have you ever watched a film, and wondered: has this been made with AI? From AI animals to face swapping, it’s getting harder to tell.

When Director Danny Boyle’s upcoming movie Ink premiered at film festivals this autumn, many viewers noticed the tell-tale signs of AI. But the director said that he made sure no actors lost out on work and that AI-generated animals could be an ethical solution to using real ones.

BBC Journalist Kesewaa Browne joins Hannah to talk about whether AI is becoming another regular film making tool and if it’s something we should be excited or worried about in cinema.

summaryZh: 本集 BBC 節目《What in the World》探討電影製作人使用 AI 技術的現況與爭議。起因是奧斯卡金像獎導演 Danny Boyle 在電影 Ink 中使用 AI 呈現特定畫面並引發討論。節目中，主持人 Hannah Gelbart 與 BBC 記者 Kesewaa Browne 探討了 AI 與 CGI 的差異、Boyle 對於保障演員薪酬與避免動物受壓迫的說法，以及預算有限的獨立創作者如何運用 AI 技術。討論亦提及影迷與業界對畫面品質下降、動畫與特效從業人員失業、版權侵權及資料中心能源消耗等隱憂，並指出 AI 目前更適合做為後製與前期企劃的輔助工具，而非完全取代人類的創意與演出。
summaryEn: This episode explores the growing use and debate surrounding AI in filmmaking, sparked by Oscar-winning director Danny Boyle's use of AI in his movie Ink. Host Hannah Gelbart and BBC journalist Kesewaa Browne discuss the differences between AI and CGI, Boyle's defense regarding actor compensation and ethical animal treatment, and how budget-constrained indie filmmakers utilize AI tools. They also address concerns from moviegoers and industry professionals about declining quality, potential job losses for VFX artists and animators, copyright issues, and the environmental impact of data centers, concluding that AI currently works best as a supportive tool for post-production and planning rather than a full replacement for human creativity.
